_source: Merged from claude-harness settings/permissions-deny.snippet.json and settings/git-hygiene.snippet.json on 2026-09-02. The rules are documented in claude-harness docs/git-hygiene.md; the project-specific TIGHTENING below is documented in AGENTS.md, which is where rule 13 says they belong.
_ss2_tightening: SS2 USED TO TIGHTEN RULE 7, AND NO LONGER DOES. `Bash(git push *)` was in ASK, not allowed, because AGENTS.md said 'Ask before pushing anything' — this repository derives its fixtures from a licensed game, so what leaves the machine was treated as the owner's call rather than a convenience. DROPPED BY THE OWNER 2026-09-12, in chat and at the approval screen, explicitly asking that pushing no longer prompt. So the project is back to harness rule 7 (push feature branches freely) and `Bash(git push *)` is in ALLOW. WHAT STILL BINDS, and it is the part that carried the actual safety: DENY beats everything, so `main`, `master`, `--force`, `-f` and `--force-with-lease` are blocked outright and no allow entry can reach them. Nothing is DENIED that has a legitimate form: a first draft also denied pushes to the working branch, which would have blocked work the owner had explicitly authorised. ONE THING TO WATCH, stated rather than asserted: `Bash(git push --delete *)` and `Bash(git push origin --delete *)` are still in ASK, and this project has NOT measured whether a broad ALLOW entry wins over a narrower ASK one in this build. If a remote-branch deletion ever runs without prompting, move those two entries into DENY — do not assume the ASK held. (The `_ss2_workflow` field below records what it cost the last time this file asserted an unmeasured precedence claim.)
_ss2_workflow: `Workflow` IS IN ASK AGAIN — RE-ADDED BY THE OWNER 2026-09-24, in chat ("fulfill the requests that you could not auto accept from the agent on the remote machine and need my word for"), on a peer session’s request (workflow-audit-44, "Options and recommendations"): it is the ADR 0001 layer that makes the owner approve each wave launch, and every other repository that adopted the ADR 0001 set carries it. HISTORY: it was DROPPED by the owner 2026-09-09 on the reasoning that the dialog bought VISIBILITY, not safety — the deterministic guard is the 6-questions/6-verifiers hard cap inside .claude/workflows/question-fanout-audit.js — and that reasoning is not withdrawn: the cap and the ONE-WAVE-AT-A-TIME rule in AGENTS.md still bind, and a session still states a wave’s spawn count in the transcript before launching it. The dialog is now IN ADDITION to them. NOTE ON AN OLD CLAIM: this field once asserted that bypass-permissions mode skips ASK rules by design; the owner reported being prompted WHILE bypass was active, so that was never true here — test it rather than citing this file.
